extracted.intended_audience: Students, faculty, and library patrons seeking guidance on creating infographics and data visualizations
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on designing, tooling, and choosing between infographics and data visualizations; includes practical tool recommendations and principles for visual storytelling and format-appropriate design. Aimed at creators preparing visuals for web, social, reports, or marketing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communicate message concisely and engagingly
rubrics_metrics.description: In today's fast-paced environment, you must communicate your message in a concise and engaging way that sets it apart from the noise. Visual content--such as infographics and data visualization--can accomplish this.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Find stories in your data, and visually communicate and share them with your audience for maximum impact. Aim for clarity and audience-appropriate emphasis so the viewer quickly grasps the main point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose between infographic and data visualization based on purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: While infographics and data visualizations both visually encode information, the terms aren’t necessarily interchangeable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the distinction provided: Infographics are developed for a particular dataset, context-sensitive, hand-crafted, and tend to be subjective (pitching a viewpoint); they are well-suited for resumes, marketing content and blog posts. Data visualizations use existing techniques with general applications, are more context-free and (largely) automatically generated, tend to be more objective and act as analytics tools, and are well-suited for dashboards and research reports. Consider your objective (persuade vs. explore) and audience when choosing form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design for storytelling and viewpoint (infographics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Infographics often introduce a clear viewpoint and use hand-picked design elements to enhance the storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberately select colors, imagery, and the order of charts to support the narrative you want to convey (example: 'Women in Tech' infographic uses traditionally feminine colors to enhance its viewpoint). Recognize that these choices make the piece context-sensitive and tied to that dataset; they are not necessarily reusable for other datasets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve objectivity and reusability (data visualizations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Data visualizations allow the viewer to assess information and draw their own conclusions and are more objective in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer standard visualization techniques and context-free presentations when the goal is exploration, comparability, or reuse across datasets (example: 'The Daily Routines of Famous Creative People' could use the same technique for other groups). Avoid editorialized design choices when neutrality is the objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice and order of charts must fit the dataset
rubrics_metrics.description: The choice and order of charts would not be compatible with any other dataset when designing a hand-crafted infographic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure each chart type and the sequence of visuals serve the specific data story; misaligned chart choices reduce clarity and can mislead. For infographics, tailor chart selection to emphasize the intended insight; for general-purpose visualizations, choose techniques that generalize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select appropriate tools and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Web Tools: Piktochart, Canva, Venngage, Animaker; The Noun Project; downloadable tools include Microsoft PowerPoint and Adobe Illustrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use templates for speed and consistency (Piktochart, Canva, Venngage). Venngage recommends templates by aesthetic and organizes templates by information type and can incorporate interactive elements. Canva supports team collaboration. Animaker creates video infographics. Campus IT provides installation instructions for desktop tools. Choose tools that match your technical skill, collaboration needs, and desired export formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Export formats and distribution considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Download infographics as png or pdf; share on social media; or publish on the web.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pick export formats appropriate for your medium (PNG/PDF for static sharing, web-friendly formats for embedding, video for animated/animated infographics). Consider platform constraints (size, resolution, interactive capability) and distribution goals (marketing vs. academic reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of icons and graphic assets
rubrics_metrics.description: The Noun Project: Large bank of downloadable icons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate icons and vetted graphic assets to improve readability and visual appeal, but ensure they support (not distract from) the message and maintain visual consistency with the overall design.
